focus: Deep-learning convolution is cross-correlation with no kernel flip. A learned kernel absorbs the flip, so the distinction changes nothing in a trained layer.
Output size per axis is floor((n + 2p - d(k-1) - 1)/s + 1). With odd k and matching same padding each output centers on its input pixel.
Groups split channels into G independent convolutions. Parameters and multiply-adds fall by G, while output shape is unchanged. Groups equal to C_in is depthwise convolution.
A 1x1 convolution is a per-pixel linear map across channels. Stacked 1x1 layers need a nonlinearity between them or they fold into one linear map.

units.title: Convolution shapes: channels, padding, stride, dilation and groups
traps: Counting padding once in the formula. D2L and PyTorch p means padding on both sides, so the total added rows are 2p.
Assuming groups change the output shape. Groups change only the weight layout and the cost, not H_out or W_out.
Reading convolution as flipped correlation and hand-flipping a learned kernel before reuse. Export the kernel as is.
units.why: Every CNN bug report starts with a shape mismatch. Channels, padding and groups decide tensor layout before any learning happens.

fit.note: D2L pooling and transposed-conv pages with UDL receptive-field sections cover both topics at derive depth, and UDL problems give checked practice.

focus: Receptive field grows by (k-1) times the product of earlier strides per layer. Stride-2 downsampling doubles the growth rate while quartering activations.
One conv layer holds C_out times (C_in/G) times kH times kW weights plus C_out biases, and costs about twice that many FLOPs per output position for the multiply-add.
Pooling has no parameters, acts per channel, and 2x2 stride-2 pooling quarters resolution. Max-pooling gives limited shift tolerance inside a window, not invariance.
A transposed convolution applies the transpose of a downsampling weight matrix. It learns an upsampling and is not an inverse of any forward convolution.

next.note: Test which of these mechanisms preserve or break translation equivariance.
Compare receptive-field growth with patch tokenization of images.

outcomes: Derive receptive-field growth across stride, kernel and dilation choices.

units.title: Pooling, transposed convolution, receptive fields and cost
traps: Quoting parameter counts as cost. FLOPs and activations scale with resolution, so doubling both sides quadruples both.
Calling transposed convolution an inverse by name. It shares only the naming pattern, so its outputs need their own checks.
Treating the receptive-field formula as uniform coverage. Center pixels feed more paths than edge pixels, so the formula gives the maximum extent.
units.why: Resolution sets both what a unit can see and what training costs. A receptive field smaller than the object and an activation bill larger than memory fail the same run.

fit.note: D2L why-conv, ResNet and augmentation pages with UDL invariance and residual chapters cover all topics, and CS231n Q1 and Q4 give checked practice.

focus: Convolution is equivariant to translation in the interior. Stride, pooling and zero-padded borders break exact equivariance, and pooling trades it for local tolerance.
Zero padding leaks absolute position. The network can learn where the whitespace border is.
A residual block fits the difference from identity, so pushing branch weights toward zero recovers a shallower net. The unraveled sum gives 2^K paths for K blocks.
Each residual addition grows activation variance under standard initialization. Per-channel batch normalization, or branch rescaling, keeps the forward stable.

next.note: Place residual paths beside dead units and normalization-axis choices.
Compare convolutional inductive bias against attention trade-offs.

outcomes: Explain what translation equivariance promises and name three mechanisms that break it: stride, pooling and padding boundaries.
Explain the residual unraveled-path view and why identity paths stabilize deep CNNs.
Measure resolution-driven time and memory across two input sizes and attribute the change.

selfTest.a: Each block can push its branch to zero and pass identity through, so the deeper net contains the shallower one. Plain stacks must fit identity through nonlinear layers.

selfTest.a: Batch statistics equal the single example, so normalization wipes out scale information and adds noise. Use the frozen running statistics instead.

units.title: Equivariance, residual CNN blocks and resolution cost
traps: Calling CNNs translation invariant. Convolutions are approximately equivariant, and only pooling plus dense layers add local invariance.
Leaving batch normalization in training mode at test time. Small or single-example batches then rescale outputs with batch noise.
Reading higher resolution as free accuracy. Activations and per-layer FLOPs grow about fourfold when both sides double, so measure before committing.
units.why: Residual structure and augmentation decide whether a deeper or larger-input model trains at all. Equivariance claims decide whether it should have been a CNN in the first place.
